events.title: Morgan Walk: River Park
events.description: Join historian Terrell L. Armistead in a special tour along the Bronx River at River Park as they share the ecological stories and community histories of the Bronx River. Led in honor of Morgan Powell, a founding member of the Bronx River Restoration and a passionate advocate for the reclamation of the Bronx River. His research has been fundamental in sharing the lesser known histories of Black and Brown Bronxites and their contributions to the eco-cultural history of NYC. You can read more of these histories can be found in detail in his blog called the Bronx Sankofa.Often much is known about the middle to Africa but less is known of the original “highways” of colonial New York, its rivers! This tour will highlight the importance of the Bronx River to indigenous Americans and its role in both enslavement and freedom for African slaves. We will also discuss the critical role of the river systems to our communities today and how Morgan Powell’s impact continues to outlive him. Note: This is part of a series of Bronx Black History Walking Tours hosted by Terrell Armistead.

events.description: This workshop introduces gardeners to practical strategies for identifying, managing, and preventing invasive plant species in community garden spaces. Participants will learn how to recognize common invasive plants found in urban gardens, understand their impact on local ecosystems, and explore effective methods for control and long-term management. The session is designed to help gardeners make informed decisions and build healthier, more resilient garden spaces. Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

events.title: In the Distortion of Celestial Privacy, a Door Left Open in the Mind
events.description: Set within the living landscape of 6BC Botanical Garden, this third annual iteration, curated by Sarah Viviana Valdez, brings together the sculptural practices of Ori Carlin, Erin Lingard, and Lizzy Chemel. The artists span materials and techniques, notably including wood-fired ceramics, metal, concrete, salvaged materials and stained glass mirages. Their works share a common sentiment toward incredible craftsmanship deriving from botany, memory, and family histories. Throughout the garden's labyrinth, each location and placement of these pieces will similarly act as an embroidery unifying the rhythms and quiet transformations to shape their own narratives. Beginning in the afternoon and unfolding toward sundown, the exhibition will culminate with closing performances by Sky Axe, Karol Konstancia with ensemble, and Fillan Fernando. These performers honor traditions of myth, folklore, songwriting, choral a cappella, and poetry. The intent is to offer gifts that extend the exhibition’s exploration of memory and storytelling. We invite visitors to wander through a space where sculpture, sound, and movement become small openings into remembrance and shared imagination. For folks who feel compelled, the curator will offer tours throughout the day. Enjoy these presented moments of pause where the private worlds we carry within us are invited to briefly open onto the garden and one another.

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
